# Justin Lo (mintychochip)

> Personal site of Justin Lo, a software engineer who publishes as mintychochip. The home page covers the portfolio, GitHub activity, token usage, a blog teaser, projects, resume, contact, and a Wordle. Posts live under /blog/.

The canonical site is https://mintychochip.dev. The home page is a client-rendered single page, so its sections are hash links. Each blog post is its own document. Prefer https://mintychochip.dev/llms-full.txt when you need the written copy instead of the rendered app.

## Site

- [Home](https://mintychochip.dev/): Justin Lo (mintychochip), software engineer, with links to GitHub, LinkedIn, and email.
- [GitHub activity](https://mintychochip.dev/#github): Contribution heatmap for github.com/mintychochip.
- [Token usage](https://mintychochip.dev/#usage): Chart of coding-agent token use.
- [Blog](https://mintychochip.dev/blog/): Index of posts.
- [Yes, That Was Me](https://mintychochip.dev/blog/the-token-gap/): First-person cross-reference to Umans AI’s “The Token Gap”.
- [Bytemill article](https://mintychochip.dev/blog/bytemill/): Interactive article on Bytemill, a schema language and compiler for binary wire formats, with the Rust compiler running in WebAssembly.
- [Projects](https://mintychochip.dev/#projects): Public repositories loaded from GitHub.
- [Resume and stack](https://mintychochip.dev/#resume): Languages and a PDF resume.
- [Contact](https://mintychochip.dev/#contact): Email justincarllo@gmail.com or send the note form, which posts to a rate-limited endpoint and emails Justin directly.
- [Wordle](https://mintychochip.dev/#wordle): Daily and practice 5-letter puzzles.

## Files

- [Resume PDF](https://mintychochip.dev/resume.pdf): Downloadable resume, saved as mintychochip-resume.pdf.
- [Usage models](https://mintychochip.dev/v1/usage/models.json): JSON of token totals by model.
- [Usage series](https://mintychochip.dev/v1/usage/series.json): JSON of daily token and cost points.
- [Full text](https://mintychochip.dev/llms-full.txt): Expanded plain-text copy of the public site.

The two usage files are static snapshots covering 2026-07-11 to 2026-08-26. `from` and `to` query parameters are ignored; filter the returned `points` by `date` yourself.
